claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'CHARACTERS' followed by the indented sub-entry 'BLOCK CONTAINS clause, VII-23'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'CHARACTERS' then '  BLOCK CONTAINS clause, VII-23'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (B-51, informative index) shows one entry per line with sub-entries indented; the transcription page-963.md has exactly that: one entry per line, sub-entries indented two spaces (e.g. 'CHARACTERS' then '  BLOCK CONTAINS clause, VII-23', '  INSPECT statement, VI-94', ...; 'CLOSE statement' with its six indented sub-entries). Every entry's text and page reference matches, and the claim concedes this. The main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy is present in the source text as indentation. The only complaint is how a Markdown renderer would collapse bare lines and that pages 961-962 use '- ' list markers instead: a formatting and rendering-consistency issue, with no content missing, misquoted or changed in meaning. Formatting-only differences are excluded, so this is not a content discrepancy.
